title: Book Two · Chapter 59: The Wrong End of the Cloth
story:
On Tuesday, Mum brings home a long piece of pale cloth. She needs to check its edge first. Then she can begin a customer's work. Ronan offers to hold one end.

“Keep it off the floor,” Mum says.

He holds the corner with both hands. Mum moves her chair back. The cloth stretches between them like a very low roof.

“Higher?” Ronan asks.

“A little. There.”

He lifts his end. Mum finds the small loose threads along the edge. She pulls one out and lays it on her knee.

Ronan watches her hands. He wants to help faster. She turns for the scissors. Ronan moves forward with the cloth.

The middle drops onto the floor.

“Stop there,” Mum says.

Ronan stops. His end is high, but the other end is still near Mum's chair. A long white fold lies under her shoe.

“I was bringing it to you.”

“I need the length between us.”

Ronan picks up the cloth. A grey mark runs across one fold. He rubs it with his finger. The mark spreads.

Mum takes the cloth from him.

“Let me see first.”

Ronan steps away. Mum checks both sides. Then she brings a clean cloth and a little water. The mark comes away slowly.

“Is it ruined?” he asks.

“No. But now this part must dry.”

He looks at the chair. Mum needs it for the rest of the work. He brings two clean chairs from the table. She lays the damp part across their backs. The cloth does not touch the wood at the sides.

“Can I still hold it?”

“After this part dries. You can clear the floor first.”

He takes the dustpan and gathers the little pieces near Mum's feet. He moves his school bag too. The room looks larger with the floor clear.

Later, Mum calls him back. This time she shows him where to stand. He waits there while she checks the edge. His arms begin to ache. He asks to put the cloth down.

Mum places it on the clean table. Then Ronan lets go.

“Thank you,” she says.

“Even after the floor?”

“You helped me now. The floor was still a problem.”

Ronan sits down and shakes his arms. Mum gives him a short strip from her own scrap bag. He ties it around his wrist like a band.

“Are you hurt?” Dad asks at supper.

“Hard work,” Ronan says.

Mum raises one eyebrow. Ronan grins and unties the strip. He puts it beside his plate before he picks up his bowl.

## 词句提示

end＝一端；cloth＝布；edge＝边缘。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan怎样让布落到地上？
2. 他怎样补救？

## 读句子

**Ronan / picks up / the cloth.** Ronan／捡起／那块布。
